item.title: More than haunted house: Re: More than haunted house
item.content:encoded:
+ Hello crit
- Bye crit

My main concern is how you're going to be pulling this off. It seems interesting, but it sounds a little cliché like Ramses pointed out.

3. Greed (Million dollars on the table. Take it or leave it.)

What happens if you take it? There should be some sort of punishment.

5. Wrath (Worst enemy in life, and/or thing that caused a horrible feeling. Supposed to trigger hate.)

Will it attack you, or something else? This idea needs to be fleshed-out further, and like I mentioned, adding some sort of punishment.

6. Envy (Person with something youve always wanted, they leave it out of their sight, working on something)

What if you take it, or what if you want something else, like a job? What would that look like?

7. Pride (Theres a 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place stand. Get on one, or help someone else on)

Interesting, but there should be a penalty for this one as well.

Overall, the idea is interesting, but… it's pretty vague and needs stuff like penalties for falling for the tricks and writing it to be less cliché-y.

item.title: My SCP Idea: Re: My SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Not an official critter.

+ Crit crit
- Tirc tirc

First off, I'm concerned that this skip is too dangerous to be interesting. It's a black hole that sucks in the Sun, and in 200 years the sun will be gone.

SCP-XXXX is an alien object that orbits the sun which sucks 1-5% of it's energy

1-5% is a ridiculous number. That means, in 200 years or more, the Sun will be completely vapori[z|s]ed. Also, wouldn't people notice?

The SCP Foundation would try to reduce the energy intake of the alien base

So, like, how? How would the Foundation send a vessel in High Solar Orbit with enough fuel to spare to rendezvous with the alien base without detection?

The Foundation would have no way to contain the object

Couldn't they just shoot it? This seems more like a job for the GOC than the SCP Foundation who specializes in anomalies. If there were anomalies in the ship, the SCP Foundation could take care of it.

Earth would be stuck in a permanent ice age.

No, all of Earth would be ice and without the Sun it'd probably be sucked into Jupiter or be flung off into space forever.

Overall, this idea is written very vaguely, and seems more dangerous than interesting.

item.title: City of normacy: Re: City of normacy
item.content:encoded:
I was thinking of something closer to a reality-anchor with memory altering effects, though thanks for pointing out the similarities that it has with 1915.

I would say that since the person moves around the city and the zone remains the same size it would be impractical for the Foundation to essentially neutralized SCPs for a couple of hours since they have no way of getting anything beyond the borders. I intend to have it so the memories and effects return after some time outside the zone related to the amount of time spent inside, but I was considering making it so any anomaly passed a certain level couldn't enter.

The focus on what supernatural phenomenon he is interested in as it relates to his abilities is something worth developing so I'll keep it in mind for the second half.

item.title: Echoes of a Monster: Re: Echoes of a Monster
item.content:encoded:
Hey there, thanks for the crit!

+ Here are my Responses +
- Close -

This feels like although I think a pattern screamer does hate all existence… they don't seem like murderous beings, so much as wanting to erase existence as a concept?

This is a completely valid point here, but these are special circumstances. I'd liken it to this situation: you've been locked in a basement, and a person begins torturing you. Do you hate the person who locked you in the basement or the person torturing you more? I, personally, would hate the torturer more, as while being locked in a basement is bad, the torturer makes it much worse. Even though I'd hate the person who locked me in the basement for enabling the torture, I'd hate the torturer more for, well, torturing me.

In this case, our world is the 'basement' for this entity; it hates being here. However, the people actively perceiving it (and their brains 'filling in the gap' of the entity, trying to make it real) are the torturer/s, and thus it hates them more. It's not murderous per se, more 'defensive' (as I said in my response to cybersqyd, it's lashing out). And in this case, lashing out is all it can do. It can't get rid of the basement, so it gets rid of the torturers.

ALSO, I don't understand this concept of someone becoming a pattern screamer… which doesn't seem to fit at all. These things are unknowable, pure hatred machines that exist outside of reality.

Again, valid point. I, uh, didn't really explain what's happening here, so I'll do that now. In my headcanon for SCP-3930, when people enter the void they become a pattern screamer, quickly losing their minds as they come to terms with the fact that they don't exist, and can't, but are being made to exist. This entity essentially acts as a smaller version of the void, in that it drags people into itself so that they cease to exist (and thus, as part of my headcanon, become a pattern screamer). It also kind of warps everything around it slightly (space trying to fill in what should be a gap, but it isn't). Hope this makes sense!

[1]I just don't think this will add much to the concept. [2]And in terms of having an enjoyable horror story, I don't think this is innovative enough. [3]Again, I don't think that Pattern Screamers fits this sorta story format at all (horror comes out of something and hunts down people in a facility).

Let's sort this out in sections:
[1] - I disagree with you slightly here. Mostly because I myself am curious about the incident mentioned in the SCP-3930 article (also found in my summary: "Given enough time, and with enough of us trying to look into this void, something crawled out of it."), and this could serve as an explanation for a presumably terrifying incident that isn't elaborated on whatsoever. However, this is only assuming I could execute this successfully, which may happen, but might not.
[2] - I mean, I can't really argue with you here. More of a matter of taste really.
[3] - To reiterate, this is building off of a serious incident that is only vaguely mentioned in the source article. While this tale mightn't be a good fit for the Pattern Screamers ordinarily, due to extraordinary circumstances I believe it does fit as an elaboration on an incident.

Basically, this Tale aims to fill in a gap in the story of SCP-3930, whilst still maintaining the whole 'unfathomable unreality' feel that is so present within it.


Anyway, thanks again for the crit, hope this helps with your concerns!

item.title: My SCP Idea: Re: My SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter or anyone with any sort of authority, but I can still read and give my thoughts.
And when reading this, they are pretty much two.

One, is that there isn't really… much to this, at all, I feel. It feels very much like a Series I object. Better yet, it feels like a 'thing that does a thing'. Yes, there is this alien object that orbits the sun and sucks up energy. So? Besides this idea probably having already been written, at least to some capacity- I'd have to check as this kind of skip isn't generally my thing- what story do you have to tell?

The central narrative sounds like what you'd expect from any SCP article where the object cannot be contained, aka the Foundation trying to remedy the effects of said object; what sets it apart? Nowadays, at least from what I see, people want more from their SCPs. They want a story. A narrative.

For instance, you could expand on where this alien object comes from; you say it is an 'alien base'. That implies to me there is an alien civilization that built it. Who are they? What do they want? Why did they build this?
If it were me, given this framework, I'd have them build this station because they are running out of energy and will all die if they don't do this. This not only provides a narrative, but also introduces the ethical question for the Foundation of 'do we let them die to save ourselves'?

All in all, I recommend you expand your idea draft! There is potential to this idea, so I think you could get something interesting out of it.
I hope this was helpful in some way!

item.title: My SCP Idea: My SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an alien object that orbits the sun which sucks 1-5% of it's energy
every decade. The Foundation would try to stop it so Earth doesn't become a frozen hellhole.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation would try to reduce the energy intake of the alien base with several different ways. The story would take over a span of 34 years with the Foundation enlisting the help of the United Nations to stop the anomalous object.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation would have no way to contain the object, and if they failed in stopping it, Earth would be stuck in a permanent ice age.

Additional Notes: I would like assistance on expanding this idea further, and if there's any issues with it, I would appreciate if you would tell me what's wrong with it.

item.title: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded: I like the suggestion of using neutrinos, as they seem to be the closest real-world equivalent to 'incorporeal energy'. As for the fading intangibility I am considering a concept of 'neutrino diffusion', similar to 'hume diffusion' in SCP-3001 and SCP-4903, wherein the intangibility is slowly being shared between the incorporeal objects and earths inner core. This would lead to a sudden absence of the inner core, causing a much more disastrous collapse than would happen if the inner core were replaced with corpses. This would also solve the debate of whether the re-materializing object would replace the solid matter or the other way round. What do you think?

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Ancient Gateway: (Seeking Greenlight) The Ancient Gateway of "Venrensorys"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:** Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Comedy

Elevator Pitch: An ancient interdimensional gateway with an unknown origin located somewhere in the underground of the North Pole, which leads to a world where lies a cosmic entity whose claimed to be a being that has existed longer than existence itself, however, with the mind of a kind-hearted average joe.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX appears to be an ancient gateway with an unknown origin. The gateway is approximately 8,849 meters constructed out of unknown solid materialize and has unknown symbols are written all over it. Any individual who walks into SCP-XXXX would lead them to a realm, where an entity whose size is inapplicably being held. The anomaly is designated as SCP-XXXX-01. SCP-XXXX-01 appears to be an inorganic entity with no human facial features, no signs of hair, eyes, nose, mouth, or eyes. Its body has entirely different physiology that is presumed to be a non-existent type.

SCP-XXXX-01 shows no signs of hostility is capable of speech, shown to have unique knowledge. It would be able to remain patiently/motionless in one place without feeling any urges/aggression over many years1. However, sometimes it would leave its place2, and will not feel disturbed if any individuals are there to observe it.

SCP-XXXX was first discovered when a group of individuals who are exploring the North Pole has reported to the authorities that they'd discovered it after finding a passage that leads deep down to its location while in the middle of finding shelter to avoid an upcoming snowstorm. As this was brought to the Foundation, they've covered it up as fast as possible and deployed a group of agents, MTF-Twilight-10, codename "Broken Stellers," was deployed with the duty is to accompany all of the witnesses out and monitor/guard the area.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP was inspired by a powerful "god" who is actually a powerful cosmic being named Venrensorys. But with a few aspects added and some changes.

Additional Notes: So, after watching through SCP-2662, I've decided to come up with this idea.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

1. Stated in the interview, it can wait patiently for even eternities.
2. Stated in the interview.

item.title: Deus Comedenti (Translation: God Eater): Re: Deus Comedenti (Translation: God Eater)
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

In other words, it's 'the greater good' theory, but in a way the reader understands the greater good on an immediate level, while also being aware of the sacrifice.

a) I think that's rather disgusting, as that's not actually how the greater good should be considered… for example the wanton sacrifice of individuals within a nation to "avoid spending 12 percent of it's GDP on imports." Not sure how dicey of a moral dilemma you've created here as its on its face, abominable.
b) this is has sorta been done alot on the wiki as well.

The 'God Eater' thing is part of the narrative. It was originally built with the intention to kill ("Eat") gods. With that in mind, it was designed to contain an entity with great power and convert it into raw unthinking energy. It just so happens that it's current users aren't aware of it's designed purpose and utilize it differently.

ok, but my point is that you need to thematically connect the anomaly to the "narrative". For example, if something broke down matter to create energy, I wouldn't assume that was used for killing gods. Typically we don't consider gods to simply be beings of matter. So what I am suggesting is you tweak this anomaly such that it is clear from the anomaly itself that there is something in it that is meant to kill the divine.

As someone fairly interesting in deicide as a narrative device, I am not sure what more you're trying to say. So the thing was meant to kill gods… ok? What thematic core to this anomaly/narrative are you trying to talk about? If its just a thing that which should kill a god… without more, I am not sure how intriguing that will be (not to mention there's plenty of that on the wiki too).

What I think you need to do is stop worrying so much about the plot and start thinking about some themes you could examine through this piece. What are you trying to talk about to the reader?

If its just "this crazy thing exists and oh isn't it a dilemma with a government using it this way" then I still have two problems:
1) the narrative does not seem connected to the anomaly. Why does it kill gods at all? Why would going into the lore of the object connect thematically to the discussion of a callous government willing to sacrifice human lives to save on annual budgets for imports?

2) As it stands, this mostly seems concerned with the discussion of the anomalous properties and the spooky implications of a callous government… but I think to stand out, it needs more. I also think the anomaly itself could be tweaked to differentiate itself from that thing that eats a life and makes energy (you can argue all you want, but why couldn't the government put in ANY organic matter to have the same effect? There's nothing inherently more potent in a human organism than others concerning the conversion of mass into energy.)
